source_title: Mexican Grand Prix qualifying: Lewis Hamilton takes pole – as it happened
source_excerpt:
🏎️ Veteran takes his first Ferrari pole; oldest since 1982 🏎️ Russell on front row; Antonelli down in fifth
14h ago Q2 eliminations – with Piastri out
14h ago Q2 eliminations – with Piastri out
Right, that’s all from me. Giles Richards’ report from Mexico City will be along shortly. Tomorrow, Beau Dure will be with you for Antonelli’s (surely inevitable) coronation.
Toto Wolff pleased for his old charge Hamilton and his current charge Russell.
He wondered if this was his first pole in Mexico. When you have a record 105, it is easy to forget one: he won from pole in 2016.
There is life in Lewis Hamilton yet. When you heard him talking about racing into the 2030s, to race at an African Grand Prix in Rwanda, it felt inspiring but perhaps overoptimistic. But there he is.
1 Lewis Hamilton 🇬🇧 Ferrari 1:16.514 2 George Russell 🇬🇧 Mercedes +0.009 3 Charles Leclerc 🇲🇨 Ferrari +0.119 4 Max Verstappen 🇳🇱 Red Bull +0.178 5 Kimi Antonelli 🇮🇹 Mercedes +0.193 6 Lando Norris 🇬🇧 McLaren +0.310 7 Isack Hadjar 🇫🇷 Red Bull +0.386 8 Liam Lawson 🇳🇿 Racing Bulls +0.515 9 Arvid Lindblad 🇬🇧 Racing Bulls +0.603 10 Pierre Gasly 🇫🇷 Alpine +0.639
And now Hamilton. “Wow. That feels great … So happy. Oh man, I’m lost for words. It’s been a really, really tough, challenging weekend … The engine issue we had yesterday … But it’s so close between us all … Wow. To have a pole here.” He is told he is the oldest driver to have a pole since Mario Andretti in 1982. “Where there’s a will, there’s a way. It’s all in the mind, honestly, for all of us … I love what I do … I dream about it. I have this amazing support around the world, these guys keeps me going, I hope they are happy today, and I hope I can deliver for them tomorrow.”
Now Russell , who is asked if he is happy. “I am, I am. It’s been a tricky few races for me and still struggling to get on top of this car, to be honest because it’s been a very difficult weekend until one lap in Q3. To almost get pole … it was very close in the end. I always know it’s in there.” His self-belief remains, despite all the frustrations.
“I was fighting with the car particularly in Q3 … There is such low downforce here.”
Leclerc speaks. “I just didn’t do a good job. The outlaps were difficult to put the tyres in the right window … A bit disappointed but to start third here is not too bad.”
So there was no false Ferrari qualifying dawn. And Russell took second – David Croft points out that the two drivers who need to win to keep the title race alive are one and two.
Hamilton does it. After Verstappen locks up on 13th then backs off, the Briton gets his first Ferrari pole, his 105th overall.
Final seconds. Here comes Antonelli. Only fifth fastest.
George Russell +0.009 in second. Leclerc third +0.119.
All going wrong for Hadjar. He misjudged the line coming into the pits. Bernie Collins says the Frenchman is all over the place mentally, complaining more than Gordon Ramsay in a Wimpy.
Bernie Collins eavesdropping on the drivers, saying their messages are full of uncertainty as to the best strategy.
Though Verstappen has that one-place penalty.
Turn 13 unlucky again for Hadjar but Verstappen gets second, +0.045.
Russell P3 , Antonelli P4, then Norris beat Hamilton at +0.177.
Leclerc puts in a 1:16.647 for provisional pole. Hamilon +0.422, a middle sector mistake.
Karun Chandhok analyses Piastri’s lap. Kerb after kerb after kerb.
Yet Norris went fastest. Top 10: Nor, Ver, Lec, Ham, Rus, Had, Ant, Lin, Law and Gas.
Blimey. Out go Hulkenberg, Colapinto, Piastri, Bortoleto, Bearman and Sainz. McLaren saved a set of soft tyres but an aborted fast lap doomed Piastri.
Relief for Hamilton. Up in third, at a minuscule +0.077.
Norris shot up to third. Piastri is 10th. Hulkenberg at seventh is the big disruptor, a threat to Lawson, Hadjar and Piastri. And HAMILTON.
Drop zone is looking like Gasly, Bortoleto, Bearman, Colapinto, Sainz and HAMILTON.
Verstappen goes fastest , 1:16.876. Hulkenberg is sixth at present.
Hamilton into the pits . Down in the drop zone at present, as is Norris, who was on used tyres initially.
Lindblad is second at +0.191, ahead of Antonelli at +0.259 and Russell at +0.307.
Charles Leclerc gets a 1:16.944, while Hamilton goes off the track at turn 13 when on a flyer, which is causing a lot of problems.
Hadjar used another set of soft tyres, which explains his margin over Verstappen.
Something weird happened to Leclerc, a power surge. The spirits of the night?
Top 10: Ham, Had, Lec, Pia, Rus, Bor, Nor, Hul, Ant, Ver.
Out go Albon , Alonso, Hirakawa, Stroll, Perez and Bottas. Hirakawa was about a second slower than Bearman but got a lot of sympathy on the team radio.
Ollie Bearman 10th fastest for Haas, his new teammate 19th.

## फॉर्मूला वन क्वालिफाइंग का रोमांचक मुकाबला

मेक्सिकन ग्रां प्री के क्वालिफाइंग सत्र में दिग्गज ड्राइवर लुईस हैमिल्टन ने शानदार प्रदर्शन करते हुए फेरारी के लिए अपनी पहली पोल पोजीशन हासिल की है। इस प्रदर्शन के साथ ही वह 1982 के बाद से पोल हासिल करने वाले सबसे उम्रदराज ड्राइवर बन गए हैं।

क्वालिफाइंग सत्र के अंतिम चरण में मुकाबला बेहद कड़ा रहा। शीर्ष दस ड्राइवरों का प्रदर्शन इस प्रकार रहा:

* **लुईस हैमिल्टन (ब्रिटेन, फेरारी):** 1:16.514
* **जॉर्ज रसेल (ब्रिटेन, मर्सिडीज):** +0.009
* **चार्ल्स ले Leclerc (मोनाको, फेरारी):** +0.119
* **मैक्स वर्स्टपेन (नीदरलैंड्स, रेड बुल):** +0.178
* **किमी एंटोनेली (इटली, मर्सिडीज):** +0.193

## ड्राइवरों की प्रतिक्रियाएं और चुनौतियां

सत्र के बाद लुईस हैमिल्टन ने अपनी खुशी जाहिर करते हुए इसे एक चुनौतीपूर्ण सप्ताहांत बताया। उन्होंने कल की इंजन से जुड़ी समस्याओं का भी जिक्र किया, जिससे पार पाकर उन्होंने यह मुकाम हासिल किया।

दूसरे स्थान पर रहे जॉर्ज रसेल ने कहा कि सप्ताहांत उनके लिए काफी पेचीदा रहा था और वह कार को संभालने में संघर्ष कर रहे थे, लेकिन क्यू-3 (Q3) के एक लैप ने सब बदल दिया। वहीं, चार्ल्स लेक्लर ने माना कि वह टायरों को सही तापमान में लाने के मामले में बेहतर प्रदर्शन नहीं कर सके और तीसरे स्थान से शुरुआत करेंगे।

## अन्य मुख्य बातें

* ऑस्कर पियास्त्री और कुछ अन्य ड्राइवर शुरुआती चरणों में ही बाहर हो गए।
* सत्र के दौरान कम डाउनफोर्स और टायरों की स्थिति से जुड़ी रणनीतिक अनिश्चितताएं देखने को मिलीं।

## मूल घोषणा की पुष्टि कैसे करें

पाठक आधिकारिक फॉर्मूला वन (Formula 1) की वेबसाइट या संबंधित खेल प्रसारण माध्यमों के जरिए परिणामों, समय और आधिकारिक घोषणाओं का सत्यापन कर सकते हैं।

en_body:
## Qualifying Highlights in Mexico City

Lewis Hamilton secured his first pole position for Ferrari during qualifying for the Mexican Grand Prix, marking his 105th career pole and making him the oldest driver to secure the top spot on the grid since Mario Andretti in 1982. 

Mercedes driver George Russell finished just 0.009 seconds behind Hamilton to claim a front-row start, while Charles Leclerc took third place for Ferrari. Max Verstappen qualified fourth for Red Bull, ahead of Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli in fifth.

## Driver Reactions and Session Incidents

- **Lewis Hamilton:** Expressed relief following a challenging weekend that included an engine issue during practice, describing himself as "lost for words" after securing pole.
- **George Russell:** Noted that despite struggling to get on top of the car amidst low downforce conditions, he managed to extract pace during his final Q3 lap.
- **Charles Leclerc:** Acknowledged disappointment with his performance, citing difficulties getting tires into the correct operating window on outlaps.

Earlier in the session, Oscar Piastri was among those eliminated in Q2 following an aborted fast lap, while Isack Hadjar encountered difficulties during the session, including an incident near the pit lane entry.

## Practical Implications and Verification

Official starting grids, race schedules, and full classification results can be verified through the official Formula 1 website (formula1.com) or via the FIA's official publication documents. Fans can catch upcoming race broadcasts through their local rights-holding sports broadcasters.
